title: Modules Are Checked Too
summary: Modules act without the owners, but the guard checks module transactions too.
lesson: Modules follow the same rulebook, and some policies accept only modules or only owners.
oneLiner: Modules act without the owners, but the guard checks module transactions too.
explain: A module is an add-on the Safe trusts to act without the owners, like an Allowance Module that pays bills.
The guard checks module transactions too, against the same rulebook. Some policies tell owners and modules apart.
The Module Allowlist accepts only the modules it lists. The Co-Signer and Extra Owner Signatures accept only the owners.
takeaway: Modules follow the same rulebook, and some policies accept only modules or only owners.

steps.label: The Allowance Module pays Dave 300 USDC
steps.note: USDC payments may come from the Allowance Module, and this one does.

steps.label: The Recovery Module pays Dave 300 USDC
steps.note: Only the Allowance Module may send USDC. The Recovery Module is not on the list.

steps.label: The owners pay Dave 300 USDC
steps.note: This rule accepts the Allowance Module only. Even the owners cannot send USDC this way.

steps.label: The Allowance Module sends Erin 1 ETH
steps.note: Anything else wants the co-signer, and a module cannot bring one. So the module is refused.
